mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.1% indicates an ultra-accommodative monetary policy environment that reduces the cost of capital for firms and stimulates risk-taking, producing positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in >50% of periods with FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.1% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate exceeding 6.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce household income and consumer spending, causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of periods with UNRATE > 6.5% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) below their 12-month moving averages indicate broad-based contraction in consumer and business activity, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of periods with both HOUST and INDPRO below 12-month moving averages (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A monetary tightening cycle with high inflation (CPIAUCSL yoy > 2.5%) and rising FEDFUNDS signals aggressive rate hikes that increase discount rates and reduce equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
regime_hint: monetary tightening cycle with high inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of periods with FEDFUNDS rising and CPIAUCSL yoy > 2.5% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate below 0.5% indicates slowing economic activity that reduces corporate earnings expectations, producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of periods with GDPC1 quarterly growth < 0.5% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, strong retail sales (RSAFS) above the 95th percentile combined with low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.5%) signals an economy approaching peak conditions, causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to profit-taking.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of periods with RSAFS > 95th percentile and UNRATE < 4.5% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: An industrial production index above 100 (relative to 2017=100) indicates robust manufacturing activity that supports corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in >50% of periods with INDPRO > 100 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly non-farm payrolls increase exceeding 200,000 (PAYEMS > 200) signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate profits, producing positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in >50% of periods with PAYEMS > 200 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).
